pr_title: *: query failed after add index / timestamp out-of-range (#28424)
pr_body:
<!--

Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:

2. *: what's changed

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #28424 

Problem Summary: Timestamp out-of-range and range optimizer incompatibility.

### What is changed and how it works?

Two issues, convertToMysqlTimestamp did set out-of-range timestamp to
Zero, when it would still be a storable/comparable KindMysqlTime.
(we only artificially limit the range of Timestamp to be compatible
with MySQL).

When this change was done,
it broke #26584 (insert of invalid timestamp succeeded),
which needed a different change in handleZeroDatetime

I think it is a corner case(very rared scenario for 'out-of-ranged' date condition and MySQL treat it as a warning instead of error:

```
mysql> select * from t02 where a != "2038-1-19 3:14:45";
Empty set, 1 warning (0.00 sec)

mysql> show warnings;
+---------+------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Level   | Code | Message                                                               |
+---------+------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Warning | 1292 | Incorrect datetime value: '2038-1-19 3:14:45' for column 'a' at row 1 |
+---------+------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```
I would treat it as 'minor' compatibility bug and we need to update the planner to fix it.

review_comments:
Is this the only case that return `types.ErrWrongValue` and can be saftly ignored?
If in some other cases `ErrWrongValue` is also returned, and we ignore the error unexpectedly

I think so.

From what I can see, the `ConvertTo(sc, tp)` with `Kind() == types.KindMysqlTime` and `tp.Tp == mysql.TypeTimestamp` can only end up in the part of types/datum.go above, that I also changed in this PR, so I cannot see any other case that would end up being ignored here.

I.e. it is only points of MysqlTime converted to Timestamp that would generate an error in `GetMysqlTime().Convert()` that would be matched here.
